composite_exponent_lift.density_consequence: The V_r-smooth integers have natural density zero. For the finite 29-prime set, all smooth exceptional strips still have density zero.
composite_exponent_lift.smoothness_consequence: For fixed r, the surviving half-exponent pairs lie in the union of the two coordinate strips where one coordinate is V_r-smooth. These strips are infinite but have natural density zero.
composite_exponent_lift.statement: If a has a prime divisor p>V_r, b has a prime divisor q>V_r, and r divides N, exponent absorption produces the forbidden prime-core equation. Hence at least one of a,b is V_r-smooth.

effective_program.family_shift: double-square summand masks reduce to finitely many one-small-prime strips plus density-zero smooth strips; the new modular targets are those asymmetric strips, one-square masks, and cross-side masks
effective_program.first_task: compute explicit V_r for r=19 and r=23, list the finitely many small prime indices p<=V_r, and attack each one-variable strip (2p,2q,r) as q varies

nonclaim: The family theorem is imported from a recent arXiv preprint rather than a peer-reviewed publication. No numerical V_r is claimed here. The theorem does not leave finitely many prime pairs: it leaves a finite union of infinite one-small-prime strips. The absorption and density-zero smoothness deductions are unconditional consequences of the imported theorem.

orientation_boundary.covered_mask: the two positive summand bases are square-masked; the right-hand base may be plain or square
orientation_boundary.not_covered: a square mask on one summand and on the right-hand side gives a difference of even powers, not Sahoo's plus equation

prime_mask_theorem.scope: p,q,r odd primes, X,Y,Z pairwise coprime nonzero integers, r in the listed set
prime_mask_theorem.statement: For each listed r, every solution has p<=V_r or q<=V_r. Thus the large-large quadrant is empty and the surviving prime pairs lie in a finite union of horizontal and vertical strips indexed by the finitely many primes at most V_r.

source.author: Satyabrat Sahoo
source.imported_corollary: For every listed prime r there is an effectively computable constant V_r such that x^(2p)+y^(2q)=z^r has no non-trivial primitive integer solution for primes p,q>V_r.
source.title: Effective Generalized Fermat equation of signature (2p,2q,r) with odd narrow class number
